blocks.text: The standard hydrogen electrode is one of several types of half-cell that can be used as a reference electrode (Figure 10.4). It consists of hydrogen gas at 101 kPa pressure in equilibrium with H+ ions of concentration 1.00 mol dm-3, and a platinum electrode covered with platinum black in contact with the hydrogen gas and the H+ ions. Platinum black is finely divided platinum, which allows close contact of hydrogen gas and H+ ions so that the equilibrium between H2 gas and H+ ions is established quickly; the platinum electrode is inert and does not take part in the reaction. Standard electrode potential values for all half-cells are measured relative to this electrode: when it is connected to another half-cell, the voltmeter reading gives the standard electrode potential of that half-cell.

blocks.alt: A glass tube dips into a beaker of 1 mol dm-3 H+ solution at 298 K. Hydrogen gas at 1 atm enters through a side arm and bubbles out through holes in a glass bell around a platinum electrode coated with platinum black, joined to a platinum wire. A box gives 2H+ + 2e- = H2, E standard = 0.00 V, the reference electrode.
blocks.caption: Standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) (original diagram after Figure 10.4).

blocks.text: The half-equation for the hydrogen electrode is 2H+(aq) + 2e- giving H2(g), E standard = 0.00 V, or equally H+(aq) + e- giving 1/2 H2(g), E standard = 0.00 V. The way the half-equation is balanced makes no difference to E standard, because the equation does not affect the tendency of the element to gain electrons; its voltage is arbitrarily fixed at 0.00 V.

blocks.prompt: What is the SHE and how is it used to measure the electrode potential of another electrode (exercise Q.6)?
blocks.explanation: It is a platinum black electrode bathed in hydrogen at 101 kPa and dipping into 1.00 mol dm-3 H+, with its half-reaction defined as 0.00 V. The half-cell to be measured is joined to it by a wire through a high-resistance voltmeter and by a salt bridge; the voltmeter reading, with its sign showing which electrode is positive, is the standard electrode potential of that half-cell.

items: SHE: H2 at 101 kPa over platinum black in 1.00 mol dm-3 H+; 2H+ + 2e- = H2 fixed at 0.00 V; inert Pt; all E standard values measured against it; the balancing of the half-equation does not change E.
